title: Vercel replaced "Develop.Preview.Ship." with "Build and deploy on the AI Cloud."
body: The original headline **"Develop.Preview.Ship."** spoke to developers who already understood the product workflow. The new headline **"Build and deploy on the AI Cloud."** signals a category shift — Vercel now positions itself as infrastructure for AI applications, not just a deployment platform. This suggests the target buyer may now include teams building AI products who need hosting, not just frontend developers optimising workflows.

title: 8 navigation items removed including "Contact Us" and "Login" — a friction-to-trial change
body: Vercel removed **"Contact Us"**, **"Contact"**, and **"Login"** from navigation while adding **"Explore Enterprise"**, **"AI Gateway"**, and **"Vercel Agent"**. This likely signals a shift from sales-assist to product-led trial. Removing login from top-level navigation suggests existing users now arrive through direct URLs or documentation, while the homepage focuses on new visitor education and category definition around AI infrastructure.

title: The meta description dropped "best frontend developer experience" for "frameworks, workflows, and infrastructure"
body: The original meta description promised the **"best frontend developer experience"** — a competitive claim. The new version says Vercel **"gives developers the frameworks, workflows, and infrastructure to build a faster, more personalized web."** This removes the superlative and adds three concrete nouns. It suggests Vercel now wants to be discovered by buyers searching for platform components, not teams comparing developer experience quality.

title: 12 new section headings appeared while only 2 were removed — this is expansion, not simplification
body: Vercel added 12 section headings including **"Build"**, **"Scale"**, **"Secure"**, **"Frameworks"**, and **"Use Cases"** while removing just 2. This is not homepage reduction — it is a site architecture expansion. The removed heading **"Clone Template"** was a single-action CTA; the new headings are navigation categories. This suggests Vercel shifted from a product demo page to a platform ecosystem site with multiple entry points.
